Simulate a deterministic SuSiE-OUT locus

Source: R/simulate.R
susieout_simulate_locus.Rd

This compact truth-known generator supports smoke tests and workflow banks. It represents recent growth through a rare-allele-enriched frequency draw, prospective causal assignment, derived-allele orientation, finite WGS panels, ancestry mismatch, and sparse/null/infinitesimal/LD-error regimes. Variants have first-order autoregressive LD, and a realistic mix of MAF, indel, imputation-quality, reference-absence and panel-monomorphism filters decides which variants are tested and which are omitted.

Usage

susieout_simulate_locus(
  seed,
  p = 40L,
  q = 10L,
  n = 1e+05,
  wgs_n = 1000L,
  architecture = c("contained", "partially_omitted", "entirely_omitted", "null",
    "infinitesimal", "ld_mismatch"),
  evolution = c("neutral", "stabilizing", "directional"),
  ancestry = c("matched", "mismatched"),
  causal_count = NULL,
  omitted_count = NULL,
  oracle_wgs = FALSE,
  infinitesimal_h2 = NULL,
  ld_mismatch_variance = NULL
)

Arguments

seed

Random seed; the same seed gives the same locus.

p

Number of tested variants.

q

Number of omitted variants.

n

GWAS sample size.

wgs_n

Size of the sequencing reference panel used to estimate LD fingerprints.

architecture

Causal architecture: all causal variants tested ("contained"), some or all omitted ("partially_omitted", "entirely_omitted"), no signal ("null"), diffuse polygenic signal ("infinitesimal"), or reference LD error ("ld_mismatch").

evolution

Selection regime used to draw effect sizes.

ancestry

Whether the reference panel matches the GWAS ancestry.

causal_count, omitted_count

Optional numbers of causal variants and of omitted causal variants; defaults depend on architecture.

oracle_wgs

If TRUE, use population LD instead of a finite-panel estimate.

infinitesimal_h2, ld_mismatch_variance

Optional polygenic variance and LD-mismatch variance; defaults depend on architecture.

Value

A list with the arguments needed by susieout_fit() (z, n, R_analysis, wgs_ld, examined_ids), the variant table variants, full-locus oracle statistics, and the simulated truth.

Examples

locus <- susieout_simulate_locus(1, architecture = "entirely_omitted")
locus$truth$causal
#> [1] "v47"
locus$truth$any_omitted
#> [1] TRUE
